headline: Measles crisis: Death toll passes 1,100 as 5 die in 24 hours
summary: Bangladesh is facing an unprecedented measles outbreak with over 211,000 cases and 1,104 deaths, marking the highest infection rate in the country's history.
details: The measles death toll in Bangladesh has reached 1,104, with five more children dying in the last 24 hours. This is the deadliest outbreak in the country's history, occurring at a time when the disease was nearly eradicated.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), a total of 211,902 people have been affected, including 190,510 with measles symptoms and 21,392 confirmed cases. This is a massive jump from just a few hundred cases in previous years.
WHO data reveals that between December last year and May this year, Bangladesh had the highest number of measles infections globally, topping the list with 42,174 cases, ahead of India and Yemen.

Public health experts, including Dr. Mushtaq Hossain and Be-Nazir Ahmed, have attributed the crisis to systemic negligence in vaccination programs during the previous interim government and subsequent failures in treatment and mass vaccination campaigns.
The human cost is devastating. In Bandarban, a couple from the Khumi community lost two sons, aged four and seven, within two days of each other, while their other two children remain hospitalized.
Experts are calling for those responsible for the vaccination gaps—which reportedly left at least 4 million children unvaccinated—to be identified and held accountable for this public health failure.
caption:
Over 1,100 children have died in a measles outbreak that has left Bangladesh at the top of the global infection list.

The measles death toll in Bangladesh has reached 1,104, with five more children dying in the last 24 hours. This is the deadliest outbreak in the country's history, occurring at a time when the disease was nearly eradicated.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), a total of 211,902 people have been affected, including 190,510 with measles symptoms and 21,392 confirmed cases. This is a massive jump from just a few hundred cases in previous years.

WHO data reveals that between December last year and May this year, Bangladesh had the highest number of measles infections globally, topping the list with 42,174 cases, ahead of India and Yemen.

Public health experts, including Dr. Mushtaq Hossain and Be-Nazir Ahmed, have attributed the crisis to systemic negligence in vaccination programs during the previous interim government and subsequent failures in treatment and mass vaccination campaigns.

The human cost is devastating. In Bandarban, a couple from the Khumi community lost two sons, aged four and seven, within two days of each other, while their other two children remain hospitalized.

Experts are calling for those responsible for the vaccination gaps—which reportedly left at least 4 million children unvaccinated—to be identified and held accountable for this public health failure.
